title: NagaWorld workers gather near Australian Embassy during ongoing strike
location: Daily action around NagaWorld and the Australian Embassy on National Assembly Boulevard, downtown Phnom Penh; VOD also reports the nearby Sisowath Quay/Sihanouk Boulevard roundabout and movement toward Aeon Mall I parking lot.
organizer: NagaWorld workers associated with Labor Rights Supported Union of Khmer Employees (LRSU); Chhim Sithar is identified as union president.
participants_original: CamboJA reports about 500 workers at the embassy gathering; VOD reports around 300–400 near NagaWorld and several hundred at the adjacent embassy site. These estimates may cover overlapping or moving groups and are not summed or averaged.
threshold_50_evidence: CamboJA reports about 500 at the embassy gathering; VOD independently reports around 300–400 workers near NagaWorld and several hundred at the adjacent strike site. Each specific estimate is clearly above 50. A different-day retrospective of up to around 1,000 is not used.

start_date.summary: CamboJA dates the gathering to Monday Jan. 3; RFA published Jan. 4 and refers to Monday’s Jan. 3 arrests.

end_date.summary: VOD reports workers leaving at about 6 p.m. on Jan. 3 after the police-cleared park and moving action; this physical end applies to the Jan. 3 gathering only, not the continuing strike.

location.summary: CamboJA places the group in front of the Australian Embassy near NagaWorld II; VOD describes the adjacent fenced strike site, the nearby roundabout, and later movement toward the Aeon Mall I parking lot.

organizer.summary: LRSU workers; article identifies Chhim Sithar as the union president.

demands.summary: Workers demanded release of detained colleagues. The ongoing strike also included reinstatement and labor-compensation demands against NagaWorld; RFA reports a demand to rehire 365 laid-off employees.

participants.summary: CamboJA estimates about 500 at the embassy gathering. VOD reports around 300–400 near NagaWorld and several hundred at the embassy site; keep source estimates separate and do not sum or average.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both event-specific sources give a turnout estimate well above 50: about 500 (CamboJA) and around 300–400 / several hundred (VOD). VOD’s around-1,000 estimate refers to crowds on some days, not specifically Jan. 3.

protester_violence.summary: CamboJA and RFA describe peaceful strike action; VOD reports no protester violence and quotes a worker describing the protest as nonviolent.

state_response.summary: Jan. 3 arrest reports differ: RFA S034 initially reports 14, CamboJA at least 15, VOD updates from 14 to 15, and RFA S015 reports 17 for Monday. Treat these as alternative counts/updates from two RFA reports and other outlets, never sum. VOD describes barricades and park clearing plus an attributed beating allegation; embedded media was not inspected. RFA S034 says hundreds of riot police were deployed to suppress the strike but does not detail a physical dispersal attempt. No killing or shooting reported.

notes: VOD reports an alleged beating in a detained worker’s account; it describes video of officers grabbing/dragging women but the media was not independently inspected, so the response is attributed rather than independently verified. Jan. 3 arrest figures vary across updates and sources (VOD 14, later 15; CamboJA at least 15; RFA 17); do not add them. CamboJA estimates about 500 and VOD around 300–400/several hundred in adjacent protest locations; keep the estimates separate. VOD’s around-1,000 figure refers to other days and is excluded. The gathering remains pending_unit because it occurred during daily demonstrations in a December-starting strike. VOD S039 also reports workers left around 6 p.m. Jan. 3, so this particular gathering is recorded as ending that day; this does not date the end of the ongoing strike or prove a month-long continuous assembly. RFA S034 provides an earlier 14-arrest account; the source accounts are not additive. Record correction: the prior episode_key was cambodia_nagaworld_strike_2021-12; E001 is now aligned with E002/E003 to identify the reported December-starting recurring public-demonstration phase. This does not decide whether the dated January gatherings merge as one episode or imply a continuous physical assembly.
open_questions: Does the Jan. 3 gathering at the Australian Embassy and adjacent NagaWorld-area sites count as a distinct episode or continuation of the Dec. 2021 NagaWorld strike?
What onset date is supported for the underlying strike?
Should the Jan. 3 public demand to release detained unionists be coded separately from the employer-directed demands?
Can another source clarify whether the different Jan. 3 arrest totals represent the same count updates or distinct groups?
Can the alleged beating be independently corroborated?

title: NagaWorld workers gather after union leaders are arrested
location: Protest site near the National Assembly, Phnom Penh; the gathering site is not located more precisely in RFA’s account.
organizer: NagaWorld workers and leaders of the Labor Rights Supported Union of Khmer Employees (LRSU).
participants_original: RFA confirms workers gathering Jan. 4 but gives no event-specific count. Its hundreds figure is cumulative since Dec. 18. LICADHO later reports about 600 workers appearing each afternoon as of Jan. 18; that later turnout is not assigned to Jan. 4.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: no source gives a Jan. 4-specific crowd size. RFA’s campaign-cumulative hundreds since Dec. 18 and LICADHO’s approximately 600 each afternoon as of Jan. 18 do not establish that 50 or more attended on Jan. 4.

start_date.summary: RFA reports three union leaders arrested and workers gathering on Jan. 4; LICADHO says Chhim Sithar was violently arrested that day while trying to join workers.

end_date.summary: The physical end of this gathering is not reported; do not infer it from the ongoing strike.

location.summary: RFA locates Chhim Sithar’s arrest near the National Assembly. LICADHO says she was trying to join striking workers in front of the Australian Embassy. The reports do not precisely reconcile the full gathering’s location.

organizer.summary: RFA identifies NagaWorld union leaders and workers; LICADHO identifies LRSU and its president Chhim Sithar.

demands.summary: Workers sought release of detained union representatives; the continuing dispute also involved NagaWorld layoffs and labor-law compliance.

participants.summary: Neither article gives an event-specific Jan. 4 attendance count. RFA’s hundreds since Dec. 18 is cumulative and LICADHO’s roughly 600 each afternoon refers to the Jan. 18 report.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Event-specific Jan. 4 turnout is absent; do not carry the cumulative strike or later daily estimate back to this date.

protester_violence.summary: The continuing demonstrations are described as peaceful; neither article reports Jan. 4 protester violence.

state_response.summary: RFA reports three union leaders arrested Jan. 4 near the National Assembly. LICADHO says Chhim was violently arrested while trying to join workers. No separate beating, dispersal, killing, shooting, accommodation or ignore response to the assembly is established.

notes: Jan. 4 is retained as a dated gathering observation, not a proven new episode onset; daily public demonstrations began in December according to contemporaneous accounts. RFA says three leaders were arrested and workers were gathering to demand their release. LICADHO later estimates roughly 600 workers each afternoon as of Jan. 18, but that figure is not carried to Jan. 4. Location accounts (near National Assembly; in front of Australian Embassy) are both attributed and not precisely reconciled. Pending event-specific turnout and unit review.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people attend the Jan. 4 gathering?
Is this dated observation a distinct protest event or part of the December-starting daily demonstrations?
Can a contemporaneous event-specific turnout estimate and exact gathering site be established?

title: NagaWorld workers continue strike during union arrests
location: NagaWorld workers’ Jan. 6 strike gathering; the CamboJA report does not specify the exact gathering site.
organizer: NagaWorld workers; the Jan. 6 CamboJA report does not name an organizer.
participants_original: CamboJA reports around 400 NagaWorld workers continued a peaceful strike on Thursday, Jan. 6.
threshold_50_evidence: CamboJA gives an event-specific estimate of around 400, clearly above 50. The gathering is one day in a December-starting daily demonstration series, so episode ownership remains pending.

start_date.summary: CamboJA published Jan. 7 and dates the around-400-worker peaceful strike to Thursday, Jan. 6.

end_date.summary: No physical end to the Jan. 6 gathering is reported.

location.summary: The report identifies NagaWorld workers but does not give a precise Jan. 6 gathering site.

organizer.summary: CamboJA identifies NagaWorld workers but names no event organizer in the article.

demands.summary: Workers sought a resolution to the ongoing labor dispute and release of union leaders and members.

participants.summary: CamboJA reports around 400 workers on Jan. 6.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The event-specific estimate of around 400 is well above 50; daily-series ownership remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: CamboJA characterizes the strike as peaceful and quotes a striker saying workers were carrying out no violence.

state_response.summary: No Jan. 6 arrest, dispersal, beating, killing or shooting is reported. The Labor Ministry sent a same-day letter about final payments for laid-off workers; the article says it fell short of demands but does not establish an agreed meeting or an event-specific response.

notes: A Jan. 6 mass gathering is documented, but CamboJA says NagaWorld employees had been striking since late November and contemporaneous sources place daily public demonstrations in December. Treat this as a January observation within an earlier campaign, not automatically a January episode onset. The same-day Ministry of Labor letter is a possible policy response but is not coded as accommodation without a documented event-specific agreement or meeting.
open_questions: Does the Jan. 6 gathering belong to a December-starting protest episode or qualify as a distinct local event?
What was the precise gathering site and physical end time?
Does the Labor Ministry letter constitute a documented accommodation of a protest demand?
